title: The True Purpose Of Classroom Management
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin distinguishes the SCM approach from stickers, tokens, lectures, countdowns, threats, narration, and bribery-based behaviorism, describing it instead as simple, honest, and quietly invisible in a well-run classroom. He poses the underlying question of classroom management's actual purpose — is it to force compliance, appease students, or build community — and answers that its true and singular purpose is to protect learning. In his framing, effective classroom management frees the teacher to focus entirely on excellent instruction and frees students to focus entirely on their academic responsibilities, maximizing time spent learning. He describes what this looks like visually: a teacher immersed in exuberant instruction, or quietly observant while students work, with no visible management machinery at all, just students striving toward higher standards.
points: SCM's approach avoids stickers, tokens, prize boxes, lectures, countdowns, threats, and narration.
The article poses and answers the central question: what is the actual purpose of classroom management?
The answer given is that classroom management's true purpose is to protect learning, not to force compliance or build community.
Effective management frees teachers to focus on instruction and frees students to focus on academics, maximizing learning time.
In a well-run SCM classroom, management itself should be invisible — visitors see only instruction and focused students.
quotes: The SCM approach to classroom management isn’t complicated. It isn’t burdensome or overbearing. It’s neither stressful nor manipulative.

It’s neither countdowns and threats and narrating students through every this and that. Nor is it a haphazard mix of “catching students doing good,” do-this-and-get-that economics, and other bribes, tricks, and manipulation.
What is the point of classroom management generally? Is it to force, subdue, and squeeze into a box?
It treats students like living and breathing people, respecting their intelligence and believing in their unlimited growth and capacity to overcome obstacles.
It’s to free the teacher to focus on great instruction and free the students to focus on their assignments and schoolwork responsibilities.

Walk into an SCM classroom and you won’t see obvious signs of classroom management. You’ll only notice the teacher, an expert in their content area, deep in the river of exacting and exuberant instruction.
